notes: SHIP v1.14.416 - THE 340ms TAP WINDOW ON THE FORGE SCENE UTILITIES. One CSS rule. Found by the full five-viewport regression matrix, not in the aisle. The scene utility cluster (grid + search, under the Forge header) sits at z-index 4 so that every overlay covers it AT REST, and the layering test asserted exactly that. But .detail-panel does not appear at rest - it SLIDES, transform over .34s - and until it has travelled far enough its own box does not yet sit over those buttons. For roughly a third of a second the panel was open, visibly moving, and a tap on the cluster still fired the loadout button. Stacking order was never the problem: the panel simply was not there yet. THE FIX IS IN CSS AND KEYED TO THE .open CLASS THE OVERLAYS ALREADY TOGGLE - a :has() rule makes the cluster inert the instant any overlay opens, rather than when it finishes arriving. The alternative was a class set by hand at five call sites (openDetail, closeDetail, openSearch, closeSearch, and three picker toggles): five chances to drift, and a sixth overlay later would silently miss it. This rule cannot be forgotten by a future caller. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE AT REST - an open overlay already owned those pixels, so this only removes a hit target that was live while its own overlay was on screen. It is not a dead control either: the cluster is inert only while an overlay visibly covers it, and returns the moment that overlay closes. :has() already appears five times in this file, and if it were ever unsupported the declaration is simply dropped and behaviour falls back to what shipped before - it cannot fail closed. HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part worth keeping: the full matrix went red on ONE project, reduced-motion, with an identical app. That failure was a TEST defect - settle() waits two animation frames, about 32ms, against a 340ms slide, so the assertion sampled the panel mid-flight and four projects passed on frame-timing luck with about 1 percent of margin. Fixing the test is what exposed the real window underneath it. THE NEW GUARD IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT A RACE: sampling the live slide cannot pin this, because how far the panel has travelled after two frames varies with frame pacing and even between the first open and the second on the same machine - measured at 241px cold and 66px warm. So the test reproduces the window GEOMETRY instead: panel open, transition suspended, parked at a position it genuinely occupies mid-slide and which does not yet cover the buttons, then probe. It also guards its own fixture - if the parked panel already covered the probe point the test would pass for the wrong reason and pin nothing. Verified red without the fix (panel top 506px, probe 112px, cluster pointer-events auto) and green with it. GATES: three inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the new commit hook. NO RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected - #forge3d-sheet is redesign-only by construction. DEVICE-VERIFY: open the Forge aisle, tap a rack to open the detail panel, and while it is sliding up try to tap the grid or search button under the header. Nothing should happen until the panel is closed again, and both buttons must work normally the moment it is.
